optNotePresets.message: Pick one goal or several. Their priorities combine; where goals overlap, their weights are averaged. A goal focused on a category takes priority over another goal’s incidental setting. Adjust how much each selected goal counts below. Some goals turn deductions into preference credits; hard score limits stay limits. Moving a category slider makes the active label Custom. Click a selected goal to remove it; Balanced clears them all.

optWeightsLede.message: 1× applies a rule as written, 0 switches it off, 2× doubles it. Goals change these weights. Press / to jump to the filter.

optNoteRateSame.message: The same switches as in the toolbar popup.

optNoteFoodOnly.message: Skips shoes, toys, cosmetics, medicine and cleaning products. A score on shampoo would imply it was judged as something you could eat. When this is on, a non-food page shows why it was skipped instead of a silent blank.

optHintFoodOnly.message: Skips shoes, toys, cosmetics and cleaning products.

optNoteWeights.message: Each category has its own default. A weight of 1.0 applies the listed rule normally; 0 switches its score effect off, and 2.0 doubles its deduction or credit before score limits. Some categories start at 0 or 0.5. Negative weights, available for selected categories, turn a deduction into a preference credit. Goal presets change these weights. Press / to jump to the filter.

optNoteAvoid.message: Separate entries with commas or new lines. Each makes its own warning and never changes the score.

optNoteExport.message: Exports every setting as a plain JSON file you can keep, edit, or move to another computer. It leaves out the master switch and your Google sign-in.

optBackup.message: Back up my settings to my Chrome account

Worked out on your computer from what was already read, under your current weights — no extra requests. Esc or a click elsewhere closes it. Clicking a score opens the product, with this on or off.

popupAutoScoreNet.message: Requests product pages from this store. On Amazon, signed in as you.

popupHoverNet.message: Requests that product page from Amazon, signed in as you.

optNoteAutoScore.message: On by default. As you scroll a results page, each result that this computer and the shared database cannot already answer is scored by requesting its product page from the Amazon store you are on: three at a time, at most 60 per results page. The requests carry your Amazon sign-in, so Amazon sees them much as if you had opened each product yourself. Turn this off and only products already read (by you, or through the shared database) show a score. Retailer previews use two public same-site requests at a time, without cookies; missing labels remain unknown. Cart ratings on every store use public product pages without cookies or referrers, two at a time within the Speed budget.

optHintAutoScore.message: Requests product pages from the store you are on. On Amazon, signed in as you.

optNoteHover.message: Off by default. Hover or tab to one result for half a second and it requests that product page from Amazon in the same way, with your Amazon sign-in. Only the result you point at.

optHintHover.message: Off by default. Requests that product page from Amazon, signed in as you.

autoNoticeTitle.message: Ingredient Check is rating these results

autoNoticeBody.message: To score a result, it requests that product's page from this Amazon store in the background, signed in as you: a few at a time, at most 60 per results page. Amazon sees each request much as if you had opened the product. You can change this at any time in the Ingredient Check toolbar popup.

popupGoalsCombined.message: Goals combined: where two set the same dial, they are averaged.

welGoalsLede.message: Pick goals that fit your preferences. They combine; overlapping priorities are averaged according to how much each goal counts. Change those priorities later in Settings. Goals guide ingredient scores; they do not predict weight loss or medical outcomes. Pick nothing for the balanced default.

welWarnLede.message: Tap any allergens or diets. Warnings sit on top of the score and never change it. They only cover the ingredient text on the page — always check the package.

welAvoidLede.message: Optional. Products containing these get a red flag, without changing the score. Tap common ones or type your own, separated by commas or new lines. Always check the package.

welOptionsLede.message: All four choices are recommended and on by default. Uncheck anything you do not want. Scoring stays on your computer. Chrome will ask for barcode lookup access when you finish. Change these choices later in Settings.

welSharedD.message: Certifications for whole foods (organic, grass-fed, origin) from tables the developer keeps. Never sends your settings or anything about you.

welDoneLede.message: Open a grocery product or search page on Amazon, Target, Walmart, Costco, Instacart, or the other store previews. Readable labels receive scores; unavailable labels are marked. You can change everything later in Settings.

optStoresLede.message: Where Ingredient Check works today, and which stores are planned. Preview stores work on the pages you open but are still being checked. A planned store is not available yet: the extension does not run there and reads nothing from it.

optRequestLede.message: Tell us which online grocery store you want next. This makes a draft in your own email app, addressed to jackson29382938@gmail.com. Nothing is sent until you press Send there, and it goes from your email address, so the recipient will see it.

optNoteTarget.message: Retailer previews rate search results and cart items from saved scores or public same-site product pages without cookies. Cart requests also omit the referrer. Automatic rating is on by default; turn it off for saved scores only. Two requests run at a time, within the Speed budget (20–60). Missing or blocked labels stay unavailable. Scores stay local; no cart data is shared. Score on hover applies to Amazon only.

optSortLede.message: On an Amazon grocery search, Amazon's own “Sort by” menu gets “Ingredient Check score: High to Low” and “Price per …: Low to High”, in the unit most listings are priced in (ounce, fl oz, pound, gallon, count…), which you can change in the side panel. Choosing one opens Chrome's side panel with this search's listings ranked; Amazon's page is left as it is. In the panel, Prioritize weighs health score, unit price, total price, rating and number of reviews, and Open in new tab shows the same list in a tab.

optSpeedBalancedD.message: Saved scores for up to 30 days. At most 60 product pages per results page. Shared readings up to 30 days old.

Ingredient Check adds a screenshot, the page you were on, your settings and your recent clicks, so it can be fixed without back-and-forth. Everything is shown below and you can leave any part out. optSharedProducts.message: Share product readings with other computers (experimental)

optSharedProductsD.message: Off by default. When on, a product another computer already read (its ingredient text, title, bullets, certifications and nutrition numbers, before any weighting) is reused instead of fetched from Amazon again, and what this computer reads is uploaded for others. Anyone can upload a reading and nothing yet checks that it is true, so a search badge or the sorted list could show a score for text that is not on the label. A product page you open is always read from the page itself. What is sent: the store and product IDs of search results this computer cannot answer, and what was read off products you scored.

optHintSharedProducts.message: Off by default. Reuses other computers' readings and uploads yours; nothing verifies them yet.

optNotePoints.message: Each product earns once a week: 20 XP at a score of 90 or more, 10 XP at 75 or more. Level n costs 100 × n XP. Points are for fun: they never change a score, are not part of a backup, and never leave this computer.

optPaceFastD.message: Five at a time, 0.1 s apart. Roughly two-thirds faster than Normal, and the most likely to be refused.
